column10: “Recién nacido”, one dose, for newborns of 2,000 g or more before leaving hospital or at the first contact with health services, preferably before 1 year.
“Recién nacido”: in the first 24 hours of life, late up to 7 days of life. A baby without this dose starts hepatitis B with the hexavalent at 2 months, so doses then fill one line earlier by count.
“2 meses”: hexavalente acelular, 1st dose; it is given whether or not the birth dose was given.
“18 meses”: hexavalente acelular, booster (dosis de refuerzo).
“18 meses”: hexavalente acelular, booster. The DPT at 4 years carries no polio.
“18 meses”: hexavalente acelular, booster. The 5th hepatitis B dose only for a child who had the birth dose; without it the booster is the 4th, and no extra hepatitis B dose is needed.
“4 años”: DPT booster (triple bacteriana), the 5th dose of the primary scheme; not later than 6 years 11 months 29 days.
“4 años”: DPT booster, the 5th dose of the primary scheme.
“4 años”: DPT booster, the 5th dose of the primary scheme (whole-cell pertussis).
“2 meses”: anti-rotavirus (RV1), 1st dose, by mouth; no dose after 7 months 29 days of age.
“4 meses”: anti-rotavirus (RV1), 2nd dose; no dose after 7 months 29 days of age. In the 2026 text “pentavalente” means the RV5 rotavirus vaccine (3 doses), not a DTP combination.
“Un año” / “12 meses”: anti neumocócica conjugada, 3rd dose.
“12 meses”: triple viral (SRP), 1st dose. A dosis cero given at 6 to 11 months in an outbreak does not count.
“18 meses”: triple viral (SRP), 2nd dose, for children born from July 2020.
